text: CHAPTER 6: TESTING

Testing in LogShield is organised around a single question: does each security and performance claim hold when it is tested? The strategy therefore combines unit tests of individual scoring factors, a labelled benchmark, an enumeration of edge cases, a root-cause analysis of observed errors, and a four-way ablation experiment designed to test whether the multi-stage, multi-factor pipeline is justified relative to simpler baselines.

text: 2. UNIT TESTS

The test suite contains 24 tests in two files. tests/test_catalog.py verifies that each pattern in the catalog correctly matches its target format and does not match safe control values. tests/test_logshield.py verifies the decision gate, the confidence model's handling of extreme inputs and the vault round-trip. All 24 tests pass as of the interim review.
3. BENCHMARK RESULTS

The benchmark was run on the 1,847-line labelled dataset as reported in Chapter 5. Precision, recall and F1-score all exceed the 0.90 targets of NFR3 and NFR4. All three latency percentiles are below 1 ms, well inside the 5 ms target of NFR1. Throughput of 12,847 lines/sec exceeds the 5,000 lines/sec minimum of NFR2.

5. PLANNED FOUR-WAY ABLATION EXPERIMENT

The core research validation is a four-way ablation experiment on a 50,000-line labelled corpus, designed to test whether the additional complexity of the multi-stage, multi-factor design is justified rather than assumed. The experiment isolates the contribution of each layer.
Table 6.3: Four-way ablation experiment design

data: Pass 1 of the Secret Classifier alone; decision gate at a single regex-match threshold
Experiment A plus the entropy factor; threshold tuned to optimise F1
Full confidence model over eight features; thresholds at 50 and 80
Experiment C plus the Preprocessor, Candidate Finder and 761 SecretBench patterns

text: The corpus will consist of 25,000 positive lines drawn from SecretBench and leaked-repository sources, and 25,000 negative lines drawn from LogHub and synthetic non-secret text. Validation protocol is five-fold stratified cross-validation. This experiment has been designed but not yet executed; it awaits the corpus-generation and weight-training run of Phase 2. 6. VAULT AND LINEAGE VERIFICATION

SecureReveal and SecretLineage are implemented and functional. The end-to-end path from detection through masking, vault write and lineage fingerprint was verified manually using the demonstration application. The vault module encrypts each masked value and stores it with the required fields. The CLI successfully performs retrieve, sprawl-report and audit-log operations. The lineage module creates a new fingerprint record on first occurrence of a secret and increments the occurrence count on subsequent occurrences from different pod UIDs, which was verified by running the demonstration application in two pods.
7. LIMITATIONS OF TESTING

Several limitations should be stated plainly. The benchmark corpus is a single 1,847-line dataset; behaviour on the 50,000-line ablation corpus and on novel secret formats is not yet established. Statistical power is limited by the rarity of real secret-leak samples in available log data. Results are conditional on the SCS decision thresholds 50 and 80, and the threshold sensitivity analysis has not yet been executed. Vault and lineage verification was manual rather than automated; automated integration tests are planned for Phase 9. The four-way ablation experiment, which is the primary research validation, has not yet been executed.
